syllabus_version.title: CBSE Curriculum for the Academic Year 2026-27

chapters.title: Exploring the Investigative World of Science

topics.title: From wonder to investigation: the root and the kite

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that Grade 8 science aims at learning how to find new facts through focused questions, simple experiments and observation.
Interpret the root and kite symbols as the balance between careful observation and creative thinking.

topics.title: The journey ahead: microbes, health, electricity, force and pressure

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise that microorganisms can be helpful or harmful and that food, exercise, medicines and vaccines keep us healthy.
Identify the heating and magnetic effects of electric current and their everyday uses.
Relate force and pressure to how air moves, from gentle breezes to cyclones.

topics.title: Particles, materials and light

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how particles move in solids and gases and classify materials as elements, compounds and mixtures.
Recognise that light reflects from mirrors and rough surfaces and bends when it passes through lenses.

topics.title: Moon, calendars, ecosystems and a planet just right for life

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that the Moon's phases depend on the positions of the Earth, Moon and Sun and helped humans make calendars.
Describe how living beings depend on their surroundings and why Earth is suited to life.
Evaluate the role of human activities and science in changing and protecting Earth's climate.

topics.title: Investigating like a scientist: why does a puri puff up?

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the factors that can be changed or controlled in a simple kitchen experiment.
Distinguish yes/no observations from measured quantities and value careful record-keeping.
Apply the rule of changing only one factor at a time while keeping other conditions the same.

chapters.title: The Invisible Living World: Beyond Our Naked Eye

topics.title: Seeing the invisible: lenses and early microscopes

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how a curved transparent lens or water-filled flask makes small things look bigger.
Describe Robert Hooke's observation of cork and his first use of the word cell.
State why Antonie van Leeuwenhoek is called the Father of Microbiology.

topics.title: Basic structure of a cell

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how onion peel and cheek cells are stained and mounted for observation.
Identify the cell membrane, cytoplasm and nucleus and state their functions.
Explain the roles of the cell wall, plastids and vacuole in plant cells.

topics.title: Variation in shape and structure of cells

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the shape of muscle, nerve and cheek cells to the functions they perform.
Explain how different cell types in the food pipe and stomach work together in digestion.

topics.title: Levels of organisation in living organisms

concepts.learning_objective: Arrange cell, tissue, organ, organ system and organism in order and classify examples.
Explain that complex organisms begin as a single egg cell, using the ostrich egg as an example.

topics.title: Microorganisms and how we observe them

concepts.learning_objective: Classify microorganisms as protozoa, algae, fungi and bacteria and as unicellular or multicellular.
Interpret observations of pond water and soil suspension under a microscope.
State why viruses differ from other microorganisms.

topics.title: Microbes around us and in cleaning the environment

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise that microbes live everywhere and explain why salt and sugar preserve food.
Explain how bacteria and fungi decompose waste into nutrient-rich manure.
Describe how microbes produce biogas and can be used to clean up pollution.

topics.title: Microorganisms in food, farming and water

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the roles of yeast and Lactobacillus in making bread, idli and curd.
Explain how Rhizobium in root nodules of legumes enriches soil with nitrogen.
Describe the importance of microalgae such as Spirulina for oxygen, food and medicine.

topics.title: The cell as the basic unit of life

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish unicellular from multicellular organisms with examples.
Compare cells of bacteria and fungi with plant and animal cells.

topics.title: Health: more than not falling sick

concepts.learning_objective: State the WHO definition of health as complete physical, mental and social well-being.
Explain how habits and surroundings affect a person's physical, mental and social well-being.

topics.title: Staying healthy: lifestyle and a clean environment

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish healthy habits from unhealthy habits in daily life.
Explain how clean surroundings, clean air and water, and good relationships support health.

topics.title: Knowing we are unwell: signs and symptoms

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish a symptom (what we feel) from a sign (what can be seen or measured).

topics.title: Diseases: causes and types

concepts.learning_objective: Identify pathogens such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, worms and protozoa as disease-causing organisms.
Classify diseases as communicable or non-communicable based on cause and spread.

topics.title: Spread and prevention of communicable diseases

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how communicable diseases spread through air, contact, food and water, and vectors.
Choose suitable preventive measures for diseases listed in Table 3.1.

topics.title: Non-communicable diseases

concepts.learning_objective: Explain deficiency diseases and chronic diseases as types of non-communicable diseases.
Relate the causes, symptoms and prevention of lifestyle diseases such as diabetes and obesity.

topics.title: Prevention: immunity and vaccines

concepts.learning_objective: Define immunity and acquired immunity.
Explain how vaccines train the immune system and why they are preventive, not curative.
Describe Jenner's smallpox vaccine and the traditional Indian practice of variolation.

topics.title: Treatment of diseases and antibiotic resistance

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that antibiotics act only against bacteria and recall the discovery of penicillin.
Explain how antibiotic resistance develops and how wise use of antibiotics prevents it.

topics.title: Magnetic effect of electric current

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field that deflects a nearby compass needle and disappears when the current stops.
Recall Oersted's 1820 discovery that electricity and magnetism are linked.

topics.title: Electromagnets: construction, poles and strength

concepts.learning_objective: Describe an electromagnet as a current-carrying coil, usually with an iron core, that behaves as a magnet.
Identify the poles of an electromagnet using a compass and predict how reversing the current changes them.
Explain how the current and the number of turns of the coil change the strength of an electromagnet.

topics.title: Lifting electromagnets and Earth's magnetism

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how lifting electromagnets on cranes lift and release iron and steel objects by switching the current ON and OFF.
Describe how currents in Earth's liquid iron core produce its magnetic field and why this field matters to living beings.

topics.title: Heating effect of electric current

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that the resistance of a conductor converts some electrical energy into heat when current flows.
Identify the factors on which the heat produced in a wire depends, such as current, material, thickness, length and time.
Identify appliances that use a heating element and the safety problems caused by overheating.

topics.title: Voltaic cell and the lemon cell

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the electrodes and electrolyte of a Voltaic cell and how a chemical reaction produces electricity.
Construct and troubleshoot a lemon cell that lights an LED.
Explain how Volta's test showed that metals and a liquid, not the frog, produced the current.

topics.title: Dry cells and rechargeable batteries

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the terminals and paste-like electrolyte of a dry cell and why it is single-use.
Explain the uses and limits of rechargeable batteries such as Li-ion batteries.
Justify why used batteries should be sent for e-waste recycling.

topics.title: What is a force and what it can do

concepts.learning_objective: Define force as a push or a pull applied on an object.
Identify how a force can start motion, change speed or direction, or change shape.

topics.title: Forces as an interaction between objects

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a force arises only when at least two objects interact, each feeling a force.
State and correctly write the SI unit of force, the newton (N).

topics.title: Contact forces and muscular force

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise contact forces as those acting through direct or indirect physical contact.
Describe muscular force and its use by humans and animals, inside and outside the body.

topics.title: Friction

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that friction arises from surface irregularities and opposes motion or attempted motion.
Relate the size of friction to the nature of surfaces and to motion through air and water.

topics.title: Non-contact forces: magnetic and electrostatic

concepts.learning_objective: Describe magnetic force as a non-contact force of attraction or repulsion between magnets.
Explain electrostatic force between charged objects and the rule that like charges repel and unlike attract.

topics.title: Gravitational force and vertical motion

concepts.learning_objective: State that gravity is the Earth's always-attractive, non-contact pull on objects.
Describe how speed and direction change when an object moves up and down under gravity.

topics.title: Weight and its measurement

concepts.learning_objective: Define weight as a force and read a spring balance using its range and smallest division.
Distinguish mass, which stays the same, from weight, which depends on where the object is.

topics.title: Upthrust, floating and sinking

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the buoyant force (upthrust) that a liquid applies upward on an object.
Predict floating or sinking by comparing the gravitational force with the buoyant force.

topics.title: Pressure as force per unit area

concepts.learning_objective: Define pressure as force per unit area, state its SI unit (pascal) and calculate it.
Explain everyday tasks by relating a smaller or larger contact area to higher or lower pressure.

topics.title: Pressure exerted by liquids

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the pressure at the bottom of a liquid column to the height of the column, not its weight.
Show that liquids exert pressure on the sides of a container and in all directions.

topics.title: Pressure exerted by air

concepts.learning_objective: Describe atmospheric pressure, its magnitude and its units, including millibar and hectopascal.
Explain a sucker and our safety under the atmosphere using a pressure difference or a pressure balance.

topics.title: Formation of wind

concepts.learning_objective: State that air moves from high to low pressure, faster when the pressure difference is larger.
Explain the sea breeze and the land breeze through pressure differences over land and sea.

topics.title: High-speed winds lower air pressure

concepts.learning_objective: Infer from the two-balloon activity that high-speed winds are accompanied by reduced air pressure.
Explain why roofs blow off in storms and how open doors, windows or holes reduce the pressure difference.

topics.title: Storms, thunderstorms and lightning

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how rising warm, moist air, cooling and condensation lead to clouds, rain and storms.
Explain charge separation in clouds and how the breakdown of air's insulation causes lightning and thunder.
Choose safe actions during lightning and explain how a lightning conductor protects a building.

topics.title: Cyclones

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how heat released by condensation, inflowing air and Earth's rotation build a cyclone, and why it weakens over land.
Describe the eye of a cyclone as the calm centre of lowest pressure surrounded by strong winds and rain.
Evaluate the damage caused by cyclones and the measures that reduce their impact.

topics.title: What matter is composed of

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that every substance is made up of a very large number of extremely small constituent particles.
Recall Acharya Kanad's ancient idea that matter is made of tiny, indivisible particles called Parmanu.
Explain how dissolving sugar in water shows that a substance breaks into particles too small to see.

topics.title: Interparticle attractions and the solid state

concepts.learning_objective: State that particles are held together by interparticle attractions whose strength decides the physical state.
Explain why solids have a definite shape and volume in terms of packing and movement of particles.
Relate the melting point of a solid to the strength of its interparticle forces of attraction.

topics.title: The liquid state

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why liquids have a definite volume but no fixed shape, using the movement and attraction of particles.
Define boiling point and distinguish boiling from evaporation.

topics.title: The gaseous state

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why gases have neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume, using the movement of their particles.
Identify liquids and gases as fluids and compare their properties.

topics.title: Interparticle spacing in the three states

concepts.learning_objective: Explain, using the syringe activity, that gases are easily compressed because their particles are far apart, while liquids are not.
Interpret volume changes on dissolving to infer that there are spaces between particles in liquids and solids.

topics.title: Movement of particles in different states

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the constant motion of water particles spreads potassium permanganate and dissolves soluble substances.
Explain how the constant motion of air particles spreads a fragrance through a room.
Relate an increase in temperature or thermal energy to faster particle movement and to the state of matter.

chapters.title: Nature of Matter: Elements, Compounds, and Mixtures

topics.title: What Are Mixtures?

concepts.learning_objective: Define a mixture and its components, and state that components keep their properties and do not react chemically.
Distinguish uniform mixtures from non-uniform mixtures using everyday examples.
Recognise alloys such as stainless steel, brass and bronze as uniform mixtures of metals.

topics.title: Is Air a Mixture?

concepts.learning_objective: Describe air as a uniform mixture of nitrogen, oxygen, argon, carbon dioxide and water vapour.
Explain how lime water turning milky shows the presence of carbon dioxide in air.
Explain that dust particles are suspended in air as pollutants and are not an integral part of it.

topics.title: Types of Mixtures and Pure Substances

concepts.learning_objective: Classify mixtures by the physical states of their components and as uniform or non-uniform.
Contrast the everyday meaning of 'pure' with the scientific meaning of a pure substance.
Explain what adulteration is, why it is done and how it harms consumers.

topics.title: Elements

concepts.learning_objective: Interpret the electrolysis of water and the tests that identify hydrogen and oxygen.
Describe elements as made of identical atoms that often combine to form molecules.
Recall facts about the number of elements, their states at room temperature and their classification.

topics.title: Compounds

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a compound is formed when elements combine in a fixed ratio and has new properties.
Infer from the heating of sugar that it is a compound of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen.

topics.title: Mixture and Compound of Iron and Sulfur

concepts.learning_objective: Compare a mixture of iron and sulfur with the compound iron sulfide formed on heating.
Identify the gases given off when the mixture and the compound react with dilute hydrochloric acid.

topics.title: Uses of Elements, Compounds and Mixtures; Minerals

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the properties of elements, compounds and mixtures to their uses in daily life and technology.
Describe minerals, including native minerals that are pure elements, and their uses.

chapters.title: The Amazing World of Solutes, Solvents, and Solutions

topics.title: Solute, solvent and solution

concepts.learning_objective: Distinguish uniform mixtures (solutions) from non-uniform mixtures using everyday examples.
Identify the solute and the solvent in solutions of a solid in a liquid and of two liquids.

topics.title: Saturated and unsaturated solutions, concentration and solubility

concepts.learning_objective: Explain when a solution is saturated or unsaturated at a given temperature.
Compare the concentration of solutions and state the meaning of solubility.

topics.title: Effect of temperature on solubility of solids and gases

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the solubility of most solids in water changes as temperature rises.
Explain how the solubility of gases such as oxygen in water changes with temperature and why it matters to aquatic life.

topics.title: Floating, sinking and density

concepts.learning_objective: Define density as mass per unit volume and use it to compare substances and predict floating or sinking.
Use the units of density and calculate relative density with respect to water.

topics.title: Determination of density: measuring mass and volume

concepts.learning_objective: Measure mass correctly with a digital weighing balance using the tare button.
Read a measuring cylinder correctly and choose a suitable cylinder for a given volume.
Find the volume of an irregular solid by water displacement and use it to calculate density.

topics.title: Effect of temperature and pressure on density

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why density generally decreases on heating, using the particle nature of matter.
Compare how pressure affects the density of gases, liquids and solids.
Explain why ice floats on water and why this helps aquatic life in cold weather.

topics.title: What are spherical mirrors?

concepts.learning_objective: Define concave and convex mirrors and identify them from their reflecting surfaces.
Explain how spherical mirrors are made and how the coated side decides the mirror type.

topics.title: Images formed by spherical mirrors and their uses

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the image in a concave mirror changes as the object moves away.
State that a convex mirror always forms an erect, diminished image.
Relate the uses of concave and convex mirrors to the images they form.

topics.title: Laws of reflection

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the incident ray, reflected ray, normal, angle of incidence and angle of reflection.
Apply the law that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection.
Explain the law that the incident ray, normal and reflected ray lie in one plane.

topics.title: Reflection of parallel beams by spherical mirrors

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why a concave mirror converges and a convex mirror diverges parallel beams.
Explain how concentrating sunlight with a concave mirror produces heat.

topics.title: What is a lens?

concepts.learning_objective: Define a lens and distinguish convex and concave lenses by their shape.
Describe how objects appear through convex and concave lenses at different distances.

topics.title: Converging and diverging lenses and their uses

concepts.learning_objective: Explain that a convex lens converges and a concave lens diverges light.
Identify everyday uses of lenses, including eyeglasses, cameras and the human eye.

topics.title: Phases of the Moon: waxing and waning

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how the bright portion of the Moon grows and shrinks over about a month, and name the waxing and waning periods.
Identify the new Moon, crescent, half, gibbous and full Moon phases in their correct order.

topics.title: Locating the Moon in the sky

concepts.learning_objective: Use the phase of the Moon to predict where and when it can be seen relative to the Sun.
Explain why the Moon rises about 50 minutes later each day.

topics.title: Why the Moon shows phases

concepts.learning_objective: Explain phases as the changing fraction of the Moon's sunlit half that faces the Earth.
Distinguish the cause of the Moon's phases from the cause of eclipses.

topics.title: Natural units of time and lunar calendars

concepts.learning_objective: Relate the day, month and year to the Earth's rotation, the Moon's phases and the cycle of seasons.
Explain why a lunar calendar drifts out of step with the seasons.

topics.title: Solar, luni-solar and Indian National calendars

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how solar calendars use leap years to stay in step with the seasons.
Explain how an intercalary month keeps a luni-solar calendar in step with the solar year.
Describe the structure of the Indian National Calendar and how it handles leap years.

topics.title: Festivals and astronomical phenomena

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why festivals based on lunar and luni-solar calendars fall on different Gregorian dates each year.
Explain why festivals based on a solar sidereal calendar fall on nearly the same date every year.

topics.title: Artificial satellites

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the typical orbit of artificial satellites and how to spot them in the sky.
Identify the uses of artificial satellites and India's major space missions.

topics.title: Habitats and their biotic and abiotic components

concepts.learning_objective: Define a habitat and recognise that habitats can be large or very small.
Distinguish the biotic and abiotic components of a habitat and the needs each meets.
Explain how different organisms coexist in one habitat by using it in different ways.

topics.title: Populations, communities and the role of every organism

concepts.learning_objective: Define a population as a group of the same kind of organisms in a habitat at a given time.
Describe a community as different populations sharing the same habitat.
Interpret how fish in a pond indirectly affect seed production in nearby plants.

topics.title: Interactions in an ecosystem; producers and consumers

concepts.learning_objective: Classify interactions as biotic-abiotic, abiotic-abiotic or among biotic components.
Define an ecosystem and identify aquatic, terrestrial and human-made ecosystems.
Classify organisms as autotrophs or heterotrophs, and consumers as herbivores, carnivores or omnivores.

topics.title: Food chains, trophic levels and food webs

concepts.learning_objective: Represent and interpret who eats whom as a linear food chain.
Identify the trophic level occupied by an organism in a food chain.
Explain how interlinked food chains form a food web.

topics.title: Decomposition and recycling of nutrients

concepts.learning_objective: Identify decomposers (saprotrophs) such as fungi and bacteria and what they do.
Explain how decomposition returns nutrients to the soil so that nothing in nature is wasted.

topics.title: Changes, balance and relationships in ecosystems

concepts.learning_objective: Trace how one change in an ecosystem leads to a chain of further changes.
Explain how competition for resources controls population size and keeps an ecosystem balanced.
Distinguish mutualism, commensalism and parasitism with examples.

topics.title: Benefits of ecosystems, threats and human-made ecosystems

concepts.learning_objective: List the benefits humans obtain from forest and aquatic ecosystems.
Identify human threats to ecosystems such as the Sundarbans and the role of protected areas.
Describe human-made ecosystems and why they need human care and management.

topics.title: Healthy ecosystems and sustainable farming

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Green Revolution and why its methods are now considered unsustainable.
Explain how overuse of synthetic chemicals and monoculture harm soil, pollinators and pest control.
Identify organic and traditional practices that support sustainable farming.

chapters.title: Our Home: Earth, a Unique Life Sustaining Planet

topics.title: Earth as a unique planet among the planets of the solar system

concepts.learning_objective: Describe how all life on Earth exists in a very thin layer at its surface.
Classify the eight planets as small rocky planets or large planets made mostly of gases.
Explain why Venus is the hottest planet and how the greenhouse effect differs from a plant greenhouse.

topics.title: Position of the Earth and the habitable zone

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why Earth's distance from the Sun lets water stay liquid and define the habitable zone.
State why the Earth looks blue from space.
Describe what scientists know and think about the possibility of life on Mars.

topics.title: Size of the Earth, its orbit and the ozone layer

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how Earth's nearly circular orbit keeps sunlight and heat steady through the year.
Explain how the Earth's size and gravity allow it to hold an atmosphere without crushing life.
Describe how the ozone layer protects living cells from ultraviolet rays.

topics.title: Magnetic field of the Earth

concepts.learning_objective: State that the Earth behaves like a giant magnet with a magnetic field.
Distinguish cosmic rays from the solar wind and explain why these particles are harmful.
Explain how the magnetic field shields the atmosphere and life on Earth.

topics.title: Earth systems that sustain life and the importance of balance

concepts.learning_objective: Identify the atmosphere, hydrosphere, geosphere and biosphere and what each contains.
Define geodiversity and explain how it creates varied habitats.
Analyse how a change in one part of the Earth system affects other parts.

topics.title: Continuity of life and asexual reproduction

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how reproduction and genes keep each kind of organism continuing and allow change.
Describe asexual reproduction in microbes and simple animals and why offspring are copies.
Give examples of plants that grow from leaf, stem or root parts.

topics.title: Sexual reproduction in plants and animals

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the role of gametes and why offspring of two parents differ from each other.
Describe pollination, fertilisation and the formation of seeds and fruits in flowering plants.
Compare fertilisation and embryo development in fish and frogs, birds and mammals.

topics.title: Threats to life on Earth

concepts.learning_objective: Name the three challenges that make up the triple planetary crisis.
Explain how burning fossil fuels causes global warming and climate change and its effects.
Describe global agreements and everyday actions that help protect the environment.
